reason: On the Create an Amazon EBS-backed AMI page the quote states that EC2 creates snapshots of the root volume and any other attached EBS volumes during AMI creation, and that you are charged until you deregister the AMI and delete the snapshots.

The quotes state that by default deregistering has no effect on the snapshots, that undeleted snapshots keep incurring storage costs, that you can optionally delete associated snapshots, and that a snapshot associated with multiple AMIs is not deleted even if specified.

The first quote states application-consistent snapshots of all EBS volumes on an EC2 Windows instance using Systems Manager command documents (linked to create-vss-snapshots-ssm); the second ties Windows applications to Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS).

The quote states verbatim up to 75 percent lower snapshot storage costs for snapshots stored 90 days or longer and rarely accessed; the context says archiving moves the snapshot from the standard tier.
The quote states that archiving converts the incremental snapshot to a full snapshot and moves it from the standard tier to the archive tier.

The quote supports the 90-day minimum and billing for remaining days rounded to the nearest hour, but the qualifier condition that a temporary restore before 90 days does not incur this charge is not in this fact's quote or context.

The quote states archiving is recommended for monthly, quarterly, or yearly snapshots and that archiving daily incremental snapshots of a single volume can lead to higher costs than keeping them in the standard tier.
The quote states restores are billed at $0.03 per GB of data restored and the example bills one time for $3, which supports the one-time charge.
The quote states it can take up to 72 hours to restore from the archive tier to the standard tier, depending on the size of the snapshot.
The quote states archived snapshots are billed at $0.0125 per GB-month with the 100 GiB example at $1.25 per month.

Under Billing for the minimum archive period, the note states a temporary restore before the 90-day minimum does not incur this charge, where this charge is the pro-rated charge for early deletion or permanent restore.

The context says AWS Backup adds enterprise-grade security and compliance to snapshots, and the quote states air-gapped vaults isolate recovery points from production and Vault Lock enforces immutability.

The quote states AWS Backup centralizes data protection, you define a single backup policy and apply it across accounts and Regions, and it supports many services including EBS, EC2, S3, EFS, RDS and Aurora.
The quote states that for EBS, AWS Backup delivers crash-consistent multi-volume snapshots coordinating point-in-time backups across all volumes attached to an EC2 instance.
The quote states verbatim that EBS volumes provide benefits that are not provided by instance store volumes.

The quote states you pay only for what you provision, storage for all volume types is charged by GB provisioned per month until released, and costs increase for additional IOPS and throughput beyond baseline.

The quote supports per-second billing with a 60-second minimum for gp3 storage, IOPS and throughput only; the qualifier condition that the pricing page states the same for gp2, io1, io2, st1 and sc1 is not in the quote or its context.

The quotes state automated AWS Backup backups of its S3 and EBS stored data, an RPO of 1 hour and RTO of 30 minutes for a 5 TB database in testing, and cost optimization through incremental EBS snapshots.
The quote states Ginkgo saved up to 90 percent of its Amazon EBS costs by reducing the size of the volumes it uses.
The quote supports the move of its most critical MySQL databases to io2 Block Express and the 256K IOPS and 64TB specifications, but the descriptor card issuer is not in the quote or its context.
The quote states NVMe reservations with Multi-Attach on io2 Block Express let Teradata switch nodes, reducing outage time from up to 20 minutes to 1 minute, an improvement of 95 percent.

The history row dated November 7, 2023 states pre and post scripts in DLM snapshot policies to automate the lifecycle of application-consistent snapshots.
The history row dated January 15, 2026 and the What's New post state a new modification can start as soon as the previous one completes, up to four per volume within a 24-hour period.

The quote supports that on February 25, 2025 you can request a completion duration for EBS-backed AMI copies, but the word extended presupposes an earlier snapshot-copy feature that this fact's quote and context do not state.
